subject: Aurora Analytics - success narrative draft (redlines & quote checks)
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@aurora-analytics.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: daniel.park@aurora-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft success story + a couple of asks

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. We reviewed the case study draft you shared (attached) and sent a PDF with inline redlines for clarity (redlines_aurora_v2.pdf). A few quick things from our side: 

- Please remove the sentence on page 2 that says “Redwood reduced our per-token cost by 10x.” That was deeper engineering shorthand — internal only.
- Can you confirm the latency numbers you call out in the second paragraph ("median tail latency 40ms")? We measure end-to-end 95th ~120ms for our interactive flows, which includes network overhead on our side.
- We want to tighten the quote from our CEO. Suggested rewording in the PDF.

We’re happy to approve once the factual items are addressed and the CEO quote is softened. If you can send a single consolidated draft with changes tracked, that would help for legal signoff.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Head of Product Marketing
Aurora Analytics

Attachments: redlines_aurora_v2.pdf (annotated), Aurora_case_draft_v3.docx

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft success story + a couple of asks

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Aurora's redlines. Priya asked us to: remove an internal "10x per-token" claim, confirm the latency wording, and tighten the CEO quote.

Marissa: can you take the copy edits and produce a single tracked-change draft? I think their suggested CEO wording is fine but please soften to "helped us reduce inference costs" rather than a numeric claim. Also update the one-line summary for the web header so it doesn't use "10x".

Laura: any legal flags on the new CEO quote or the product phrasing? Also want to be sure we don't commit to SOC2 / compliance language we can't substantiate — they haven't asked for that, but their drafts sometimes imply it.

Link to working doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cAuroraDrafts (they're watching this folder).

Thanks — I’d like to respond to Priya with an updated draft by Monday and a short list of confirmed metrics.

Best,
Aditya
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft success story + a couple of asks

Thanks, Aditya — I pulled the PDF redlines into the doc and made the following changes (attached as Aurora_case_draft_v3.docx):

- Removed the explicit "10x per-token cost" sentence and replaced with: "significantly lowered inference costs through batching and KV caching optimizations."
- Reworded the latency line to: "observed median generation latency of ~40ms at the serving layer; end-to-end interactive latency experienced by Aurora was higher due to client-side network and orchestration (~120ms)."
- Revised CEO quote per their suggestion and softened the language: "Redwood helped us scale reliable inference while materially improving cost efficiency."
- Added a short footnote clarifying the test conditions for any microbenchmarks (server-side only).

I also updated the web summary to remove any numeric multiplier. Attached: Aurora_case_draft_v3.docx and a one-page change log.

Attachments: Aurora_case_draft_v3.docx, change_log_aurora_v1.txt

Next step: Laura, if legal signs off, I can push this back to Priya for final CEO approval.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft success story + a couple of asks

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few legal/ops notes after a skim: 

- The revised latency phrasing is good. Please append: "Measured on Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 under the customer's workload profile; results may vary by deployment." That protects us from variability claims.
- Confirm we are not including any guaranteed SLA statements beyond what’s in our standard docs.
- Trademark: when referencing "Aurora" use the full company name on first mention and then "Aurora" thereafter — their PR wants this but we should follow.
- The CEO quote change is fine, but we need explicit written signoff from their CEO (Priya copied Daniel; please request CEO sign-off in the reply).

No security or SOC2 language in the story — if they want us to state SOC2 compliance we need evidence and a permissions check with security.

I’ll mark legal approved pending the CEO sign-off and the one-line deployment caveat being included.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
